answer: Lagoon escrow with delayed settlement. Each new identity posts a refundable deposit that is released only after a fixed delay, and the agent must keep answering a rotating challenge whose results are shared as a signal across peers. Cloned identities pay the deposit repeatedly and wait through every delay, while honest agents recover funds once. The prism of peer checks exposes duplicates that fail the challenge. Cost to attacker: full deposit plus delay per clone, scaling linearly with identity count.
